parameters.content:
## Immigration Case Status Tracker

### How it works

1. Runs daily. Polls USCIS's public case-status lookup for every open case in your tracker sheet.
2. When a case's status changes, sends the client a plain-English update (no legal interpretation of what it means) through the compliance guardrail.
3. Separately, watches for cases with a Request for Evidence: tracks the response deadline (87 days by default) and alerts staff as it approaches -- this alert goes to staff, never the client.
4. Every case's row is updated with the latest status regardless of whether an email was sent, so the sheet is always the source of truth.

**Verify the USCIS endpoint and status-parsing pattern before deploying.** USCIS's public case-status page is not a documented, versioned API -- it's an HTML page not intended for programmatic use, and its markup can change without notice. Test a real receipt number live and confirm `USCIS_STATUS_REGEX` still extracts the status correctly before turning this on for real clients.

**This only ever reports status -- it never interprets what a status means for the case, predicts outcomes, or gives legal advice** (ABA Op. 512).

### Setup steps

- [ ] Create the case tracker sheet (see deploy guide for exact columns).
- [ ] Set up the Bar-Compliance Guardrail (NTC-33) if not already deployed.
- [ ] Verify the USCIS case-status endpoint and regex live with a real receipt number (see deploy guide) -- do this BEFORE activating.
- [ ] Set the required n8n Variables: FIRM_NAME, FIRM_FROM_EMAIL, FIRM_ATTORNEY_EMAIL, GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID, IMMIGRATION_CASE_TRACKER_SHEET_ID.
- [ ] Optionally tune RFE_RESPONSE_WINDOW_DAYS, RFE_ALERT_LEAD_DAYS, USCIS_CASE_STATUS_ENDPOINT, USCIS_STATUS_REGEX.
- [ ] Activate the workflow.

## Poll status and update clients

Checks every open case's status daily and emails the client only when something actually changed -- through the compliance guardrail, since this reaches a client.

## RFE deadline alerts — a second, independent branch

Alerts staff (never the client) as a Request for Evidence response deadline approaches.

nodes.name: Poll USCIS Case Status Daily
nodes.notes: Runs once a day (default 6am) -- matches the 24-hour poll interval this template is designed around. Polling more often provides no benefit since USCIS itself doesn't update case status faster than daily.

nodes.name: Read Case Tracker Sheet
nodes.notes: One row per case your firm is tracking. Feeds both the daily status poll and the RFE deadline check below.

nodes.name: Filter To Active Cases
nodes.notes: Skips cases already marked closed/approved/denied in the tracker sheet -- no reason to keep polling USCIS for a resolved case.

nodes.name: Poll USCIS Case Status
nodes.notes: USCIS's public case-status lookup -- no API key, but also not a documented/versioned API. Verify this endpoint still responds this way with a real receipt number before relying on it.

nodes.name: Parse USCIS Status From Response
nodes.notes: Reads the case row by name, not $json, since the USCIS response in between replaces $json with the raw page text.

nodes.name: Determine Status Change And RFE
nodes.notes: Compares the freshly polled status against the sheet's last known status, and separately tracks whether this case just entered or exited a Request for Evidence.

nodes.name: If Status Changed
nodes.notes: Only emails the client when the status actually moved -- a daily poll finding no change stays silent.

nodes.name: Build Plain-English Client Status Update Email
nodes.notes: Reports the status only -- deliberately does not interpret, predict, or advise on what the status means for the case (ABA Op. 512).

nodes.name: Check Compliance Before Status Update
nodes.notes: Every client-facing update goes through the Bar-Compliance Guardrail for opt-out and disclaimer handling before it sends.

nodes.name: If Update Approved
nodes.notes: The guardrail blocks the send if this client has opted out.

nodes.name: Send Client Status Update Email
nodes.notes: Reads the email content by name, not $json, since the guardrail call in between replaces $json with its own response.

nodes.name: Skip Update Email For Opted-Out Client
nodes.notes: This client has opted out -- the status is still recorded in the tracker, they just don't get emailed.

value.last_status: ={{ $('Determine Status Change And RFE').item.json.status_changed ? $('Determine Status Change And RFE').item.json.new_status : $('Determine Status Change And RFE').item.json.last_status }}
value.last_status_at: ={{ $('Determine Status Change And RFE').item.json.status_changed ? $('Determine Status Change And RFE').item.json.last_checked_at : $('Determine Status Change And RFE').item.json.last_status_at }}

nodes.name: Update Case Tracker Row
nodes.notes: Always updates the row with the latest poll result, whether or not the status changed or the client email actually sent -- the sheet stays the source of truth either way.

nodes.name: Compute Approaching RFE Deadlines
nodes.notes: Flags any unresolved RFE whose 87-day (default) response deadline is within RFE_ALERT_LEAD_DAYS -- a missed RFE deadline can mean automatic denial, so this never silently skips one.

nodes.name: Build RFE Deadline Alert Email
nodes.notes: Internal staff alert only -- an RFE deadline is calculated from a fixed response window, never a legal determination of the actual filing deadline.

nodes.name: Send RFE Deadline Alert Email
nodes.notes: Goes to firm staff, not the client -- no compliance guardrail wrap needed.

main.node: Build Plain-English Client Status Update Email
Skip Update Email For Opted-Out Client
